data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Elyssa was a sea goddess who protected sailors and mariners. In the New Testament, Elyssa (Helen of Troy) is mentioned as the woman whose beauty launched the Trojan War. In Christianity, Elyssa can represent steadfastness and the power of God over the sea and storms. The name Elyssa carries the meaning “Goddess of the seas” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Elyssa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the seas and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Elyssa total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

This association gives the name a rich cultural significance, reminding us of the power and beauty of the sea and the importance of safety and protection in seafaring.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christian tradition, the name Elyssa can represent steadfastness and the power of God over the sea and storms. The name can serve as a reminder of the divine protection and guidance that can be found even in the midst of turbulent circumstances. It can also inspire a sense of peace and tranquility in the face of chaos and uncertainty. May those named Elyssa be encouraged by the stability and steadfastness of their name, trusting in the power and love of God to carry them through any storm.

historical_references.reference: According to medieval legend, Elyssa was a Greek handmaiden who was caught up in the persecution of early Christians. She was accused of being a Christian and was sentenced to be burned at the stake. As she was being taken to her execution, she picked up a crucifix and began to pray. The fire miraculously did not harm her, and she was eventually freed and baptized. The name Elyssa is believed to have derived from the Greek word for 'goddess', as she was seen as a protector and a symbol of faith.

Another historical reference for the name Elyssa comes from the Greek island of Lesbos. During the Byzantine period (circa 4th-15th centuries AD), there was a famous monastery dedicated to Saint Euphemia, which was located in the city of Eressos. The name of the monastery was sometimes referred to as the Monastery of Saint Elyssa. The name Elyssa may have been derived from the Greek word for 'island' or 'islet', as the monastery was located on a small piece of land off the coast of Lesbos.
